sections.h2: Where are Oceana County deeds recorded?
sections.html:
Deeds for Oceana County property are filed with the Register of Deeds, whose office is inside the Hart courthouse. Reach it at (231) 873-4158 or write to P.O. Box 111, Hart, MI 49420. Voters elect the register to a four-year term, and the post makes that person the official keeper of the county's land records.

Behind the counter sits an index of everything recorded, plus the original plats for each subdivision. Local governments call on the office for liber and page numbers, instrument numbers and parcel descriptions taken from those plats. UCC financing statements may be filed there as well, and the register chairs the County Plat Board that signs off on new subdivisions.

You can request copies or file a document in person or by post, as long as the fee is enclosed. Enclose a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself. Adding a daytime phone number lets staff call about a defect instead of returning the paper. The department page also links an online official records search.

sections.h2: What is Oceana County, Michigan, like for a property seller?
sections.html:
Oceana is a rural West Michigan county on the Lake Michigan shore, with Hart serving as seat and largest incorporated community. Michigan created it in 1840 and organized it in 1855. Of its 1,306 square miles, 794 are water and 512 are land.

The economy began with logging, as timber moved down the White River, and turned to farming. Asparagus is the signature crop, enough that the county bills itself the Asparagus Capital of the World, and Hart hosts the National Asparagus Festival. Part of the Manistee National Forest lies within the borders.

Before settlement, the land belonged to the Ojibwe, and in the 1850s the federal government moved about 1,400 Odawa here from Ionia County. Population climbed from 496 in 1840 to a peak of 26,873 in 2000, and the 2020 count was 26,659, so the county has been steady for twenty years.

  • US 31 follows the western side, passing Rothbury, New Era, Shelby, Mears, Hart and Pentwater.
  • M-20 crosses the south from US 31 near New Era toward Hesperia.
  • M-120 climbs north from the Muskegon and Newaygo corner to meet M-20 at Hesperia.
  • Shoreline road B-15 runs from the south county line up to Pentwater.

Mason, Lake, Newaygo and Muskegon counties adjoin it on land. Recording and transfer tax stamps belong to the county holding the parcel, so make sure the property lies in Oceana before you send a deed here.

sections.h2: What do the latest Census figures show for Oceana County housing?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts Oceana County at 27,177 people for July 2025 and 16,115 housing units. Of 10,419 households, owners hold 84.5%, and the typical owned home is worth $190,100. Rent at the median is $759 a month, and owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,280.

Nearly a quarter of residents, 24.9%, are over 65, and 15.8% identify as Hispanic or Latino. Only 136 building permits were issued during 2025. Prices here sit far below the Detroit suburbs, so the dollar cost of transfer tax and other percentage-based charges is lower even though the rates match.

Stability stands out: 91.8% of people had not changed addresses in the prior year, and the county has 1,554 veterans. Broadband reaches 83.1% of households, which affects how comfortably a seller can handle e-signing and electronic recording from home.

sections.h2: What does the Oceana County register charge for recording?
sections.html:
State law, at MCL 600.2567, fixes recording at $30 for any document regardless of length. A charter county may set a different schedule by ordinance, so phone the Oceana office for the price list before you mail a check.

Fees a Michigan register of deeds may charge, MCL 600.2567
ServiceAmount
Record one document$30.00
Each extra instrument covered by an assignment or discharge$3.00
Page of a copy$1.00
Certification of a recorded document$5.00
Grantor/grantee search, each year covered$0.50, with a $5.00 floor
Filing or looking up any other paper$1.00

Pay when you hand over the document. Electronic submissions have one business day after receipt, and the statute gives government agencies and tax foreclosure filings separate payment schedules.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies when an Oceana County house sells?
sections.html:
Two Michigan acts tax a deed's value, and the register's page cites MCL 207.505 for the county share and MCL 207.526 for the state share. Transfers worth $100 or more owe both: 55 cents per $500 block to the county and $3.75 per block to the state, counting any partial block as a full one. The seller or grantor is the taxpayer.

The fraction rule shows up in a sale at the county's $190,100 median. That value breaks into 381 blocks of $500, because the last $100 counts as a whole block. County tax is $209.55, state tax is $1,428.75, and the pair comes to $1,638.30. Swapping two properties triggers tax on each deed, measured by the true value of what each deed conveys.

  • State the full consideration on the deed, or file a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit alongside it.
  • The affidavit costs nothing to file, but the deed must say it is being filed.
  • Write any exemption you claim on the instrument.
  • A parcel lying in two counties pays each county on its share of the price.

sections.h2: Which rules does a deed have to meet for Oceana County?
sections.html:
The register publishes a checklist built on Michigan's recording statute, MCL 565.201 and neighboring sections. A document that misses a point gets returned, so read the list before you sign.

  • Signatures are originals, and typed, stamped or printed names appear below them.
  • Notary names match the signature names exactly.
  • A grantee address, by street or post office box, appears on each deed or assignment.
  • The drafter's name and address are on the document.
  • A Michigan judge, court clerk or notary acknowledges anything that conveys or burdens real estate.
  • A survivor clause needs a certified death certificate or other proof of death.
  • Court orders arrive certified and sealed by the court clerk.

The page layout has its own checks. Keep the top 2.5 inches of the first sheet blank and half an inch clear on every other edge. Print in black on white stock that weighs 20 pounds or more, in type of 10 points or larger, and use sheets between letter and legal size. The first line of print must name the recordable event in a single statement.

sections.h2: Can Oceana County deeds be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, through Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile or Indecomm Global Services. Sign up with one provider to begin. The register answers e-recording questions at (231) 873-4158.

A title company closing your sale can say whether it files through one of these services. For a family transfer or a paper deed, deliver the original to the courthouse or mail it with the fee and a return envelope.

faqs.q: What number reaches the Oceana County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: (231) 873-4158. The office sits in the Hart courthouse, and the post office box is 111, Hart, MI 49420.

faqs.q: Will the register accept a deed sent by post?
faqs.a: Yes, with enough fees enclosed. Add a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself, and a phone number so staff can resolve any question about the paperwork.

faqs.q: What does recording one document cost in Oceana County?
faqs.a: State law sets $30 per document, whatever the page count. Because a county schedule can differ, confirm the figure with the office before you send payment.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to file the transfer valuation affidavit?
faqs.a: No. The deed has to state that the affidavit is being filed, and the affidavit has to disclose the total consideration.

faqs.q: Who owes the Michigan transfer tax when an Oceana County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller or grantor does, according to the register's page. The county levy is 55 cents and the state levy is $3.75, each applied to every $500 of value.
